 Order

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 23.10.2008 passed by IInd MACT, Ratlam in Claim Case No.07/2008 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the death of Vardu, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,32,000/- along with interest.

The breakup of the compensation amount is as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Loss of dependency -Rs.1,20,000/-
 (Rs.1500x12x10(multiplier) - 1/3 )
 Loss of consortium -Rs.10,000/-
 Funeral expenses -Rs.2,000/-
 ------------------
 TOTAL Rs.1,32,000/-
3.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Smt.Bijali Bai & Ors. vs Bherulal & Ors.

Tribunal is on the lower side.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

So far as income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.1500/- per month is concerned, in the considered opinion of this Court, the same was on the very lower side, therefore, considering the minimum wages the income of the deceased is assessed as Rs.3000/- per month.
Keeping in view the verdict of the apex court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi - 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC), 10% income is also added as loss of future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi - 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as consortium is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded only a sum of Rs.10,000/- under this head.
Considering the number of dependence of the deceased, the consortium amount is also assessed as Rs.2,40,000 (i.e. Rs.40000x6).

The Tribunal has awarded only a sum of Rs.2000/- towards other conventional heads which is also on the lower side,
therefore, a sum of Rs.15000/- each is awarded under the head of funeral expenses and loss of estate.

Thus, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Loss of dependency -Rs.2,37,600/-
(i.e. Rs.3000 10% FP=3300 - 1/3 personal expenses =2200 x 12 x 9 (multiplier) Loss of consortium -Rs.2,40,000/-
 Funeral expenses -Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.15,000/-
 --------------
 TOTAL Rs.5,07,600/-
7.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.5,07,600/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.1,32,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.3,75,600/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.3,75,600/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months, the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
10.. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part and to the extent indicated herein above.
